crime_highlights: Mr. Townsend punches Ms. Litzen-Parson in the head with the result that she falls to the ground
Mr. Townsend responds by punching Mr. Riley in the head, dropping him to the ground
Mr. Townsend forcefully and brutally stomps on Mr. Riley's head
Mr. Riley suffered ongoing concussive symptoms, a fracture to his cheekbone, a non-displaced fracture of his nose and two broken teeth
Mr. Rafiq lost a front tooth and also had a concussion and a non-displaced fracture of his nose
rationale_highlights: the systemic and background factors affecting aboriginal people and the impact on Mr. Townsend of his aboriginal heritage, were also relevant
in recognition of Mr. Townsend's aboriginal status and the need to balance denunciation and deterrence with rehabilitation
note: Appeal court summarises trial judge; Aboriginal status reduced sentence to two years new time.

crime_highlights: he and another person accosted the complainant, pulled him from his car and badly beat him
a skull fracture and bone fragments in his cheek, back and chest
His injuries required hospitalization and left him with seizures and daily headaches that persist
As well he suffered disfigurement to his face and head.
rationale_highlights: Courts must take judicial notice of the history of colonization and racism that has embedded systemic difficulties and social and economic deprivation within the Aboriginal community
the judge correctly considered the effect the appellant's troubled childhood had on his moral culpability
The judge then correctly also considered what effect the appellant's Aboriginal heritage had on his moral culpability and the appropriateness of the sentence
placed little weight on it in the particular context of this offence
note: Court holds Aboriginal heritage was considered but given little weight.

crime_highlights: Ms. Florence did not tell Ms. Burt she had stabbed Mr. Milne
she saw Mr. Milne lying on the floor with blood around his head
he had been stabbed ten times and cut four times
Two of the stab wounds were life-threatening; one to his chest, the other to his back.
rationale_highlights: that denial was one of the causes of the alcoholism that likely caused the abuse of her mother
had the potential to assist in her rehabilitation in the future
she gave weight to both Ms. Florence's Aboriginal heritage and her prospects for rehabilitation
Absent those factors, it is likely that she would have imposed a parole-ineligibility period greater than 12 years
note: Court of Appeal infers trial judge gave weight to Aboriginal heritage; Gladue report was flawed.
